questions.question: What does 'AI Security' cover, according to the guide?
options: Only antivirus software that uses no AI at all
AI being used both as a tool for attackers and as a tool for defenders
Only the security of self-driving cars
Only AI being used to write marketing content
questions.explanation: AI as attacker aur defender — new arms race. Deepfake phishing, AI-generated malware ek taraf; anomaly detection, automated response doosri taraf.

questions.question: Which of these is listed as an example of 'AI as attacker' in the guide?
options: Deepfake phishing using cloned voice or video
Automated threat response in a SIEM
questions.explanation: AI as Attacker: Deepfake phishing (voice/video clone), AI-generated perfect spear phishing emails, automated vulnerability discovery.

questions.question: WormGPT (2023) was notable for what capability?
options: Providing free cybersecurity training to students
Generating phishing emails and malware code with no ethical restrictions, available on the dark web
questions.explanation: WormGPT: ChatGPT jaise AI model, sans restrictions — phishing emails, malware code generate karta tha, dark web pe subscribe kiya ja sakta tha.

questions.question: Which of these is listed as an example of 'AI as defender' in the guide?
options: Anomaly detection and automated threat response
questions.explanation: AI as Defender: Anomaly detection, automated threat response, behavior analytics (UEBA), log analysis at scale, vulnerability prediction, smart SIEM.

questions.question: An attacker uses an AI tool to clone a CEO's voice and calls an employee requesting an urgent wire transfer. What category of AI-enabled threat does this represent?
questions.explanation: Deepfake phishing (voice/video clone) — exactly is scenario ko match karta hai, AI ka attacker-side use.

questions.question: What does 'root' mean in Linux/Unix systems?
options: Superuser — full, unrestricted access to the system
A basic guest-level account with minimal access
questions.explanation: Linux/Unix mein 'root' = superuser = god mode. Windows mein 'Administrator'. Full unrestricted access — files delete, users create, services install.

questions.question: What is 'vertical privilege escalation'?
options: Encrypting a file with a stronger algorithm
Moving laterally across a segmented network
Going from a low-level user account to admin/root access
questions.explanation: Vertical privilege escalation (user → admin) — attackers hamesha root access tak escalate karne ki koshish karte hain.

questions.question: What is the Windows equivalent term for 'root' access on Linux/Unix systems?
questions.explanation: Linux/Unix mein 'root', Windows mein 'Administrator' — dono terms same level of full access refer karte hain.

questions.question: A low-privilege user account on a compromised server exploits a vulnerability to gain full administrator control of the entire system. What is this called?
questions.explanation: Low-level user access se root access tak jaana — yehi vertical privilege escalation ki definition hai, ek critical vulnerability class.

questions.question: What is the goal an attacker typically has once inside a system with limited access, according to the guide?
options: Immediately leaving the system without further action
Escalating to root access for full control
questions.explanation: Attackers always try to escalate to root — full control ke liye yeh unka common goal hota hai.

questions.question: How do properly designed systems store passwords, according to the guide?
options: As plain text for easy recovery
Only in the user's memory, never stored
As a hash, not as plain text
questions.explanation: Proper systems passwords plain text nahi store karte — hash store karte hain. SHA256('password123') = fixed string.

questions.question: Which tools does the guide mention as GPU-accelerated password cracking tools?
questions.explanation: Hashcat, John the Ripper — GPU-accelerated password cracking. RTX 4090 = 300 billion MD5 hashes/second.

questions.question: Which hashing algorithms does the guide specifically recommend NEVER using for passwords?
options: Any algorithm at all is forbidden
questions.explanation: Never use MD5 or SHA1 for passwords — instead bcrypt, Argon2, scrypt use karo, jo specifically slow hashing ke liye designed hain.

questions.question: What is the purpose of adding a 'salt' before hashing a password?
options: Making the password visible in plain text for recovery
Removing the need for a password entirely
Speeding up the hashing process significantly
questions.explanation: Salt (random string add karo before hashing) — rainbow tables defeat karo, ek same password bhi alag hash produce karega alag salt ke saath.

questions.question: The password 'password' gets cracked instantly, while 'Tr0ub4dor&3' takes years to crack using the same tool. What does this illustrate?
options: GPU-based cracking tools don't affect crack time at all
Password complexity and length dramatically affect crack resistance
Only password length matters, complexity is irrelevant
All passwords are equally vulnerable regardless of complexity
questions.explanation: 'password' = cracked instantly, 'Tr0ub4dor&3' = years — yeh directly demonstrate karta hai ki complexity aur length crack resistance ko kitna affect karte hain.

questions.question: What is a DoS (Denial of Service) attack?
options: A method for securely managing passwords
An attack that only steals data, never disrupts availability
An attack from a single source designed to make a service unavailable
A type of encrypted backup process
questions.explanation: Single source se service unavailable karna — DoS: single machine se attack, DDoS: distributed sources se.

questions.question: Why is a pure DoS attack described as easier to block than a DDoS attack?
options: Because DoS attacks are illegal but DDoS is not
Because DoS attacks never actually reach the target server
Because DoS attacks always use encrypted traffic
Since it comes from a single machine, you can simply ban that one IP
questions.explanation: DoS: Single machine se attack. Easy to block (IP ban karo). Limited bandwidth/impact — DDoS is is se harder hai kyunki hazaron sources hote hain.

questions.question: Which type of DoS attack exhausts server resources using half-open TCP connections?
questions.explanation: Protocol (TCP SYN flood — half-open connections exhaust karo), Volumetric (flood karo), Application layer (HTTP requests — web server crash).

questions.question: Which type of DoS attack works by sending HTTP requests that crash the web server directly at the application layer?
questions.explanation: Application layer (HTTP requests — web server crash) — each type needs different defense, according to the guide.

questions.question: A single machine floods a small website with traffic, and the site's admin quickly identifies and blocks that one IP address, resolving the issue within minutes. What made this attack relatively easy to mitigate?
options: It was a DoS attack from a single source, not a distributed DDoS
It was a credential stuffing attempt
It was actually a supply chain attack
questions.explanation: DoS single machine se attack hai isliye easy to block hai — ek IP ban karke resolve ho sakta hai, DDoS ke against yeh mushkil hota.

questions.question: What does UEBA (User & Entity Behavior Analytics) do?
options: Manages a company's cloud storage costs
Uses machine learning to baseline normal behavior and flag deviations
questions.explanation: Machine learning se user aur entity ka normal behavior baseline karo, phir deviations flag karo.

questions.question: In the guide's example, what does UEBA flag when 'John usually logs in 9-5 from India'?
options: Any login during normal business hours
questions.explanation: John usually 9-5 India se login karta hai. Suddenly 3am Russia se login = red flag — behavioral deviation detect hoti hai.

questions.question: What kind of threats can UEBA detect that signature-based tools might miss?
options: Only known malware with existing signatures
Only threats from outside the organization, never insiders
Zero-day threats, through unusual behavior rather than known signatures
questions.explanation: Zero-day threats bhi pakad sakta hai unusual behavior se — signature se nahi, behavior se detect karta hai.

questions.question: Which of these is listed as something UEBA can detect, according to the guide?
questions.explanation: Detects: Insider threats, compromised accounts, data exfiltration, privilege abuse — sab behavior deviation ke through pakde jaate hain.

questions.question: An employee who normally downloads a few files a week suddenly downloads the company's entire customer database at 2am on a Sunday. A security tool automatically flags this as unusual. Which technology is most likely responsible?
questions.explanation: Unusual access times, large data downloads, off-hours logins — exactly UEBA jo behavior baseline se deviation detect karta hai.

questions.question: What technology is required to access the Dark Web?
options: A standard web browser with no special software
A VPN alone, without any other tool
questions.explanation: Dark Web: Tor needed, anonymous, not indexed by Google — ek hidden part of the internet.

questions.question: Roughly what percentage of the internet does the guide say makes up the 'Surface Web'?
questions.explanation: Surface Web: Google index karta hai (4%), Deep Web: not indexed (90%), Dark Web: Tor needed, not indexed (6%).

questions.question: Which analogy does the guide use to describe the layers of the internet?
options: A phone book listing every website
A library with locked and unlocked sections
An ocean, with the Dark Web compared to the Mariana Trench
questions.explanation: Ocean ki tarah — Surface = visible waala hissa, Deep = underwater, Dark = Mariana Trench, reach karna mushkil, genuinely dangerous creatures wahan.

questions.question: Who originally created the Tor Project, according to the guide?
questions.explanation: Tor Project made by US Navy — journalist whistleblowers, censorship bypass jaise legitimate uses bhi hain, dark web = mostly evil nahi hai.

questions.question: Which of these is listed as a legitimate use of the Dark Web, according to the guide?
options: Censorship bypass for activists in restrictive countries
questions.explanation: Dark web = journalist whistleblowers, censorship bypass (Iran, China activists), privacy enthusiasts — 'not all evil'.

questions.question: What is a Cyber-Physical Attack?
options: A purely theoretical scenario that has never actually happened
A cyberattack whose consequences manifest in the physical world
An attack that only steals digital data with no real-world impact
A type of physical break-in with no digital component
questions.explanation: Cyber attack jiske physical consequences hain — power grids off karna, traffic lights hack, water poison — digital command = physical disaster.

questions.question: In the Florida Water Treatment attack (2021), by how much did the hacker increase the sodium hydroxide levels?
questions.explanation: Hacker ne Oldsmar city ke water treatment plant ka SCADA system access kiya aur sodium hydroxide 111x badha diya — drinking water poison attempt, operator ne catch kiya.

questions.question: Who ultimately prevented disaster in the Florida Water Treatment attack case, according to the guide?
options: A firewall automatically blocked the attacker
The FBI intervened remotely in real time
A human operator noticed and reversed the change
questions.explanation: Operator ne catch kiya, disaster averted — is case mein human vigilance ne bade damage ko roka.

questions.question: Which growing trend does the guide say is increasing the risk of cyber-physical attacks?
options: The decline of internet usage overall
A reduction in the number of IoT devices
questions.explanation: Smart cities, connected infrastructure, Industry 4.0 — jitna zyada connectivity, utna zyada attack surface.

questions.question: An attacker gains access to a city's water treatment SCADA system and attempts to alter chemical dosing levels to dangerous amounts, but a vigilant operator catches and reverses it in time. What type of attack was attempted?
questions.explanation: Digital command = physical disaster attempt — exactly cyber-physical attack ki definition, jaisa Florida water treatment case mein hua.

questions.question: What does Cloud IAM control?
options: Only physical access to a data center building
Only which fonts are used in a cloud application
Access to cloud provider resources like S3 buckets, EC2 instances, and databases
questions.explanation: Cloud provider ke resources (S3, EC2, databases) tak access control — roles, policies, permissions, kaunsa service kaunsa resource access kar sakta hai.

questions.question: What is the most common cause of cloud breaches, according to the guide?
questions.explanation: Misconfigured Cloud IAM = most common cloud breach cause — yeh directly Capital One jaise breaches se bhi connect hota hai.

questions.question: Which of these is a recommended Cloud IAM best practice, according to the guide?
options: Sharing long-lived access keys among all team members
Not using the root account for daily use
Disabling MFA on the root account
Using the root account for all daily tasks
questions.explanation: Least privilege — root account daily use mat karo. MFA on root. Roles use karo instead of long-lived access keys.

questions.question: Which logging feature does the guide recommend enabling for cloud access auditing (specifically for AWS)?
questions.explanation: CloudTrail logging enable karo — regular access review ke saath, yeh AWS-specific auditing tool hai.

questions.question: A junior developer is given the cloud root account's long-lived access key for a simple daily task instead of a scoped, temporary role. What best practice does this violate?
options: Using roles instead of long-lived access keys, and not using root for daily tasks
questions.explanation: Roles use karo instead of long-lived access keys, root account daily use mat karo — is scenario mein dono best practices violate ho rahi hain.

questions.question: What is a Data Breach?
options: Sensitive or confidential information ending up in unauthorized hands
A type of encrypted backup process
questions.explanation: Sensitive, confidential ya protected information unauthorized parties ke hands mein jaana — intentional ya accidental dono ho sakta hai.

questions.question: What is the average cost of a data breach, according to the guide (citing IBM 2023 data)?
questions.explanation: Average cost: $4.45 million (IBM 2023) — yeh statistic guide mein specifically diya gaya hai.

questions.question: Within how many hours must a data breach be reported under GDPR, according to the guide?
questions.explanation: GDPR notification 72 hours mein required — yeh ek strict regulatory deadline hai companies ke liye.

questions.question: A 2018 report suggested that 1.1 billion Indians' Aadhaar data was accessible for how much money via WhatsApp?
questions.explanation: Report aaya ki 1.1 billion Indians ka Aadhaar data accessible tha for ₹500 via WhatsApp — UIDAI ne deny kiya, par investigation ne serious vulnerabilities found.

questions.question: Which of these is listed as an aftermath consequence of a data breach, according to the guide?
options: No impact on customer trust whatsoever
questions.explanation: Stock price drop (avg 7.5%), customer trust loss, class action lawsuits, regulatory fines, executives fired — sab aftermath consequences hain.

questions.question: What is a Cybersecurity Framework?
options: A physical lock mechanism for server rooms
A structured approach to managing cybersecurity risk
questions.explanation: Structured approach to manage cybersecurity risk — building code jaisa, ek common language aur standard approach deta hai.

questions.question: What are the 5 core functions of the NIST Cybersecurity Framework (CSF)?
questions.explanation: NIST CSF: 1. Identify (assets, risks samjho), 2. Protect, 3. Detect, 4. Respond, 5. Recover — 5 core functions.

questions.question: Which framework specifically documents actual adversary tactics as a matrix?
questions.explanation: MITRE ATT&CK: Adversary tactics matrix — actual attack techniques documented, ek unique framework focused on attacker behavior.

questions.question: Which analogy does the guide use to describe a cybersecurity framework?
options: A CCTV control room watching cameras
A building code for architecture — a common standard so engineers don't build inconsistently
A movie ticket used once for entry
questions.explanation: Building code for architecture jaisa — alag-alag engineers alag-alag sochein to inconsistency, framework ek common language aur standard approach deta hai.

questions.question: Which framework specifically focuses on web application vulnerabilities?
questions.explanation: OWASP Top 10: Web vulnerabilities — ISO 27001 international standard hai, MITRE ATT&CK adversary tactics, CIS Controls top 18 security actions.
